equity.level_reason: Homelessness and incarceration (SES) appear only as descriptors of one patient's TB risk factors and setting; no group-specific results exist.

level_alternative.reason: With two cases, these are clinical history items rather than an equity reading; the SPD effectively only describes the patient.

ev.q: His risk factors for TB included previous work as a medical orderly, homelessness, and multiple incarcerations.
A 53-year-old incarcerated man received 600 mg (6.7 mg/Kg) RIF
A 59-year-old woman received 600 mg (7.2 mg/Kg) RIF and 2000 mg (24 mg/Kg) PZA daily

equity.equity_measurement: Two individual cases; homelessness and incarceration are named as TB risk factors for one patient, not as causes of a disparity.

notes: Laboratory values are set against normal ranges only to characterize each case clinically; no population comparison is made, so comparison is none. Serology and PCR rule out viral hepatitis and are not procedures.
